prompt: Multiplying two columns of 500,000 rows: `iterrows` 11.2 s, `apply(axis=1)` 2.8 s, `df["a"] * df["b"]` 0.002 s. Why is the last one so far ahead?

choices.text: It uses several cores where the other two use one
choices.why: It is single-threaded; the difference is the per-row object and the interpreter.

choices.text: It reuses a cached result, since exactly the same two columns were multiplied before
choices.why: Nothing is cached between the three runs.

choices.text: It is lazy, so the multiplication has not happened when the timer stops
choices.why: The result is materialised; nothing is deferred.

choices.text: A vectorised operation with a slightly slower dispatch

choices.text: A compiled loop over the rows, which is why it beats `iterrows` by about four times
